Malik, al-Hasan ibn Salih, al-Layth, and al-Shafi'i said: whichever of them refuses is subject to the hadd: he for the accusation and she for adultery. From al-Hasan: if he invokes li'an and she refuses, she is imprisoned. From Makhul, al-Dahhak, and al-Sha'bi: she is stoned. The legislation of li'an is evidence that adultery and accusation are not disbelief in the one who commits them, contrary to the Khawarij who say that it is disbelief on the part of the liar of them both, because of the deserving of the curse from Allah and the wrath. Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you say): why was the woman who invokes li'an specified to be sworn with the wrath of Allah? (I say): as an intensification against her, because she is the origin of wickedness and is followed in her enticement. For this reason she was mentioned first in the verse of flogging. What supports this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Khuwaylah: "Stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah."

﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse. Al-Suddi said: His grace (fadl) is His favour (minnah), His mercy (rahmah) is His blessing (ni'mah). Ibn Salam said: His grace is Islam, and His mercy is the concealment (of sins).

When the Exalted explained the ruling on one who accuses chaste women and wives, it was part of His grace and mercy that He made li'an (the oath of mutual imprecation) a means to concealment and to averting the hadd (the prescribed punishment). The answer to *law-la* (لَوْلا, "were it not for") is omitted. Al-Tabrizi said: Its estimated answer is "you would have been destroyed," or "He would have exposed you," or "He would have hastened punishment upon you," or "the liar would have been made manifest" (لَتَبَيَّنَ الكاذِبُ). Ibn Atiyya said: "He would have exposed the fornicators by an easier means than this," or "He would have seized them with a punishment from Him," and other meanings of this kind, which the omission of the answer necessarily requires one to estimate, because the answer is left ambiguous.

(p. 436) ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather it is good for you. For every man among them is the requital of the sin he earned, and for him who took upon himself the greater part of it there is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of one another and say, "This is a manifest lie"?﴾ ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses to it? And since they did not bring the witnesses, they are, with Allah, the liars.﴾ ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾ ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it a trivial matter, while with Allah it is grave.﴾ ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a monstrous slander"?﴾ ﴿Allah admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ ﴿And Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. **The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of these verses is well known and is recorded in the Sahih. Al-ifk means lying and fabrication. It was said: it is slander (buhtan) that you do not perceive until it suddenly surprises you. Al-'usbah means the group, and its discussion has already passed in Surat Yusuf (peace be upon him). The phrase "from among you" (minkum) means from among the people of your religion and those who belong to Islam; among them are hypocrites and among them are Muslims. Apparently, the predicate (khabar) of "inna" is "a group from among you," and "from among you" is in the position of a qualifier (sifah), as al-Hawfi and Abu al-Baqa said. The clause "do not think it" (la tahsabuhu) is a resumed sentence (mustaʾnaf). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "'usbah" is in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "jaa'u" (they came), and the predicate of "inna" is in His saying "do not think it," the estimate being "inna fi'l al-ladhina" (indeed, the act of those who...). This is more coherent in meaning and more beneficial than taking "'usbah" as the predicate of "inna." End of quotation.**

**The group is 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of hypocrisy; Zayd ibn Rifa'ah; Hassan ibn Thabit; Mistah ibn Uthathah; Hamnah bint Jahsh; and whoever supported them from among those whose names are not mentioned. The address "do not think it" is to those among the believers who were distressed by it, especially the people of the incident. The pronoun in "do not think it" apparently refers to the slander, and according to Ibn 'Atiyyah's parsing, it depends on the omitted element he estimated as the subject (ism) of "inna." It was said that it may refer to the slander, to the verbal noun implied by "they came," and to the grief that touched the Muslims. The meaning is: "do not think that disgrace will befall you because of it; rather it is good for you," for the clearing of innocence, the reward for patience over that harm, and the exposure of the slanderers' lie.**

**It was said that the address in "do not think it" is to the slanderers, and that it is good for them because this mention was a swift punishment like an expiation, and because some of them repented. This view is weak because of His later saying, "for every man among them is the requital of what he earned of sin," meaning the recompense of what he earned, which corresponds to the extent of his involvement in it: some of them laughed, some remained silent, and some spoke. "Kasaba" is used for good, because its attainment suffices without indicating effort in it. "Kasaba" may also be used in both senses.**

**"And for him who took upon himself its greater part" (wa-alladhi tawalla kibrahu): the well-known view is that this is 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and the great punishment is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was said that it is what befell Hassan of the loss of his sight and the paralysis of his hand, and that this came from 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy because of his persistence in enmity toward the Messenger (ﷺ) and his seizing of opportunities against him. A foul statement is reported from him about that; I have kept my book free from mentioning it and my pen from writing it. May Allah disfigure him. It was said that "the one who took upon himself its greater part" is Hassan, and the painful punishment is his blindness and his flogging (hadd), and Safwan's striking him on the head with a sword, and he said to him:**

Beware the edge of the sword from me, for I am a youth; when I am provoked, I am no poet.
But I defend my sanctuary and guard myself against the baseless liar who shoots at the innocent of appearances.

**Hassan recited lines praising the Mother of the Believers and showing his innocence of what was attributed to him. They are:**

Chaste and dignified, never suspected of any doubt, she wakes up hungry for the flesh of the heedless.
The wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance and the noble virtues.
The noble lady of the clan of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, whose noble endeavors and glory never fade.
Refined, whom Allah has perfumed in her chamber and purified from every blemish and falsehood.
If what was conveyed to you of me is what I said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And how could it be, when my love for her as long as I live, and my support, are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?
For him are ranks high above the people, whose excellence the assault of the boastful cannot reach.

**The well-known view is that Hassan, Mistah, and Hamnah were flogged. It was said that 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy was also flogged, and one of the poets of that age mentioned him in verse. It was said that Mistah was not flogged. It was said that 'Abdullah was not flogged. It was said that no one was flogged in this incident; but this contradicts the text.**

**"Flog them with eighty lashes" (fa-jlidūhum thamānīna jaldatan) [24:4]. Juxtapose this with the statement that the hadd (the prescribed punishment) is imposed only upon confession or evidence, and that its implementation is not restricted to reporting, just as the killing of the hypocrites is not restricted, though Allah has informed of their disbelief.**

**The majority (al-Jumhur) read "kibrahu" with a kasrah on the kaf. Al-Hasan, 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Zuhri, Abu Raja', Mujahid, Abu al-Barahsam, al-A'mash, Humayd, Ibn Abi 'Ablah, Sufyan al-Thawri, Yazid ibn Qutayb, Ya'qub, al-Za'farani, Ibn Miqsam, and Surah (from al-Kisa'i) read it. Mahbub (from Abu 'Amr) read it with a dammah on the kaf. "Al-kibr" and "al-kubr" are both verbal nouns of "kabura al-shay'," meaning the thing became great; but the Arabs' usage of the dammah is not for age. One says, "This is the kubr of the people," meaning their eldest in age or rank. In the hadith about the story of Huwayyisah and Muhayyisah: "The kubr, the kubr" (meaning: let the eldest speak). It was said that "kubruhu" with a dammah means most of it, and with a kasrah means the initiation of the slander. It was also said that with the kasrah it means the sin.**

**"Why, when you heard it" (lawla idh sami'tumuhu): this is an exhortation to think well, a rebuke, and an instruction in good conduct. Apparently the address is to the believers, excluding those who took upon themselves the greater part of it. It was said that they may be included in the address, and that there is in it a reproach, that is, denial was obligatory upon them. Then, after the address, the discourse shifted to the third person and from the pronoun to the explicit noun. The construction was not "you thought well of yourselves (bi-anfusikum khayran) and said" but rather it was done to intensify the rebuke through a shift (iltifat) in discourse, and to explicitly use the word "believers." This signifies that sharing in faith requires that no believer accept from a critic or slanderer a statement against his brother. It also indicates that when a believer hears a report about his brother, the right course is to base the matter on a good opinion, and to say, on the basis of that opinion, "This is a manifest lie," clearly affirming his brother's innocence, as one certain and aware of the true state of affairs would say. This is good conduct. As for "by themselves" (bi-anfusihim): it means that the excellent believing men and women should measure this matter against themselves; if it is far-fetched for them, they judge that it is even more far-fetched for one better than them. It was said that it means "by their mothers," and it was said "by their brothers," and it was said "by the people of their religion." He also said, "Do not find fault with yourselves" [49:11], and "greet one another" [24:61], meaning: let none of you find fault with another, and let some of you greet others.**

**"Why did they not bring four witnesses for it" (lawla ja'ū 'alayhi bi-arba'ati shuhada'): Allah made the distinction between a false accusation and a true one to be the presence or absence of four witnesses. If they do not bring them, then in Allah's judgment and law they are liars. This is a rebuke and censure of those who heard the slander and did not strive to repel and deny it, and an argument against them based on what is manifest and clear in the Law: that the accuser must be deemed a liar without evidence, and must be punished.**

**"Had it not been for Allah's bounty" (wa-lawla fadlu Allah): that is, in this world, through blessings, including the respite granted for repentance. "And His mercy upon you" refers to the Hereafter, through pardon and forgiveness. "Would have touched you" (lamassakum): the punishment for what you plunged into of the story of the slander. One says "afāḍa fī al-ḥadīth," "indafa'a," "hadaba," and "khāḍa," all meaning to plunge into speech.**

**"When you received it" (idh talaqqawnahu): the governing element (ʿāmil) for "idh" is "lamassakum." The majority read "talaqqawnahu" with a fatḥah on the three letters and a shaddah on the qāf. Al-Bazzi doubled the tā' and the Nahwiyyun and Hamzah assimilated (idghām) the dhāl of "idh" into the tā'. That is, one of you takes it from another. One says "talaqqā al-qawl," "talaqqanahu," and "talaqqafahu." The original form is "tatalaqqawnahu," and this is the reading of Ubayy. Ibn al-Sumayfa read "tulqūnahu" with a ḍammah on the tā' and qāf and a sukūn on the lām, the present tense of "alqā." From him also: "talqawnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and qāf and a sukūn on the lām, the present tense of "laqiya." 'A'ishah, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Isa, Ibn Ya'mur, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read with a fatḥah on the tā', a kasrah on the lām, and a ḍammah on the qāf, from the Arab saying "wa-laqa al-rajul," meaning he lied, as transmitted by the lexicographers. Ibn Sidah said: they brought a transitive verb as evidence for an intransitive one. But in my view he meant "yalqūnahu fīhi" (they throw it into it), the preposition having been dropped and the verb attached directly to the pronoun. Al-Tabari and others relate that this word is derived from "al-walaq," which is hastening with one thing after another, like number after number, or speech after speech. One says "walaqa fī sayrihi" if he hastened in his journey. He said: "Camels of 'Īs brought him from Syria, hastening (yaliq)." Ibn Aslam and Abu Ja'far read "ta'liqūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā', a hamzah with a sukūn after it, and a kasrah on the lām, from "al-alaq," which is lying. Ya'qub, in the transmission of al-Mazini, read "tilqūnahu" with a kasrah on the tā', a yā', and a fatḥah on the lām, as if it were the present tense of "waliqa" with a kasrah on the lām, just as they say "tijal," the present of "wijilta." Sufyan said: I heard my mother read "idh tathqafūnahu," meaning the present tense of "thaqifa." He said: her father used to read according to the letters of Ibn Mas'ud.**

**The meaning of "with your mouths" (bi-afwāhikum) is that you turn it over in them without knowledge, because a known matter resides in the heart and then the tongue expresses it; and this slander has no locus except the mouths, as He said: "They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts" [3:167].**

**"And you think it trivial" (wa-tahsabunahu hayyinan): that is, a small sin. "And it is with Allah" great, among the major sins. He attached the touching of punishment to three sins: receiving the slander, speaking it, and considering it trivial. Then He began rebuking them for speaking it, and it was obligatory upon them, when they heard it, not to utter it. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how is it permissible to separate "lawla" and "qultum" (you said)? I say: adverbs have a status, namely their placement among things as if they were the things themselves, since they occur within them and are not separate from them; so what is permissible in them is permissible in other things. End of quotation. What he mentioned about the particles of urging suggests that this is particular to adverbs, which is not so; rather it is permissible to front the object before the verb. You say "lawlā Zaydan ḍarabta" (why did you not strike Zayd) and "halla 'Amran qatalta" (why did you not kill 'Amr). Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit of fronting the adverb so that it becomes an intervening element? I say: the benefit is to show that it was obligatory upon them to refrain from speaking of the slander at the very moment they heard it. Since mention of the time is more important, fronting was required. If you ask, what is the meaning of "yakūnu" (it is/it befits), when the sentence without it would be "mā lanā an natakallama bi-hādhā" (it is not for us to speak of this)? I say: its meaning is "mā yanbaghī wa-yaṣiḥḥu," that is, "it is not fitting for us to speak of this, and it is not valid for us." Similarly, "mā yakūnu lī an aqūla mā laysa lī bi-ḥaqqin" (it is not for me to say what is not my right). "Subḥānaka" (Glory be to You) expresses wonder at the magnitude of the matter. If you ask, what is the meaning of wonder in the word of glorification? I say: the origin of that is that Allah is glorified when one sees something amazing among His creations; then it became common, until it was used for everything that is amazing. Or it is to declare Allah far above the violation of the sanctity of His Prophet (ﷺ), as was said regarding this matter. End of quotation.**

**"Allah admonishes you that you return" (yaʿiẓukumu Allāhu an taʿūdū): that is, concerning returning to it. One says, "I admonished so-and-so about such-and-such, and he left it."**

**"If you are believers" (in kuntum mu'minīn): an urging for them to take admonition and a stirring, because it is the nature of the believer to keep away from what disgraces him of ugly things. It was said that "an taʿūdū" (that you return) is an object of purpose (maf'ūl li-ajlihi), meaning: out of dislike of "an taʿūdū."**

Allah makes the signs clear to you, that is, the proofs of His knowledge and wisdom through what He sends down to you of legislation (shara'i'), and teaches you of good conduct (adab), and admonishes you with healing exhortations.

Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and in the Hereafter. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: the reference is to Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those who resemble him.

"Among those who believe" is due to their enmity toward them. The painful punishment in this world is the prescribed hadd (the fixed legal penalty), and in the Hereafter it is the Fire. The apparent meaning of "Those who love that indecency should spread" is general, covering every slanderer, whether a hypocrite or a believer. Attaching the threat to the love of its spreading is evidence that intending depravity is itself depravity. Allah knows who is innocent and who is guilty, and the inner secrets of affairs, and the wisdom behind His concealing you and the severity of the threat. Al-Hasan said: by this threat and curse He meant the hypocrites, who intended and loved to harm the Messenger (ﷺ), and that is disbelief, and its doer is cursed. Abu Muslim said: they are the hypocrites, whom Allah threatened with punishment in this world at the hands of the Messenger through striving against them, as in His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73]. Al-Karmani said: "Allah knows their lie, while you do not know it," because it is unseen. The answer to (law la, "if not") is omitted, meaning: He would have punished you.

"And that Allah is Compassionate" in exonerating you, "Merciful" in accepting the repentance of whoever repents among those who slandered. Ibn Abbas said: the address is to Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, but the apparent meaning is general.

But I defend my sanctuary and guard myself against the baseless liar who shoots at the innocent of appearances.

**Hassan recited lines praising the Mother of the Believers and showing his innocence of what was attributed to him. They are:**

Chaste and dignified, never suspected of any doubt, she wakes up hungry for the flesh of the heedless.
The wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance and the noble virtues.

Refined, whom Allah has perfumed in her chamber and purified from every blemish and falsehood.
If what was conveyed to you of me is what I said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And how could it be, when my love for her as long as I live, and my support, are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?
For him are ranks high above the people, whose excellence the assault of the boastful cannot reach.

"And that Allah is Compassionate" in exonerating you, "Merciful" in accepting the repentance of whoever repents among those who slandered. Ibn Abbas said: the address is to Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, but the apparent meaning is general.

For every man among them is the requital of the sin he earned, and for him who took upon himself the greater part of it there is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of one another and say, "This is a manifest lie"?﴾ ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses to it? Glory be to You! This is a monstrous slander"?﴾ ﴿Allah admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ ﴿And Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. Apparently the address is to the believers, excluding those who took upon themselves the greater part of it. It was said that they may be included in the address, and that there is in it a reproach, that is, denial was obligatory upon them. Then, after the address, the discourse shifted to the third person and from the pronoun to the explicit noun. This signifies that sharing in faith requires that no believer accept from a critic or slanderer a statement against his brother. This is good conduct. As for "by themselves" (bi-anfusihim): it means that the excellent believing men and women should measure this matter against themselves; if it is far-fetched for them, they judge that it is even more far-fetched for one better than them. It was said that it means "by their mothers," and it was said "by their brothers," and it was said "by the people of their religion." He also said, "Do not find fault with yourselves" [49:11], and "greet one another" [24:61], meaning: let none of you find fault with another, and let some of you greet others.**

Allah makes the signs clear to you, that is, the proofs of His knowledge and wisdom through what He sends down to you of legislation (shara'i'), and teaches you of good conduct (adab), and admonishes you with healing exhortations.

**The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of these verses is well known and is recorded in the Sahih. Al-ifk means lying and fabrication. It was said: it is slander (buhtan) that you do not perceive until it suddenly surprises you. Al-'usbah means the group, and its discussion has already passed in Surat Yusuf (peace be upon him). The phrase "from among you" (minkum) means from among the people of your religion and those who belong to Islam; among them are hypocrites and among them are Muslims. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "'usbah" is in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "jaa'u" (they came), and the predicate of "inna" is in His saying "do not think it," the estimate being "inna fi'l al-ladhina" (indeed, the act of those who...). This is more coherent in meaning and more beneficial than taking "'usbah" as the predicate of "inna." End of quotation.**

**The group is 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of hypocrisy; Zayd ibn Rifa'ah; Hassan ibn Thabit; Mistah ibn Uthathah; Hamnah bint Jahsh; and whoever supported them from among those whose names are not mentioned. The pronoun in "do not think it" apparently refers to the slander, and according to Ibn 'Atiyyah's parsing, it depends on the omitted element he estimated as the subject (ism) of "inna." It was said that it may refer to the slander, to the verbal noun implied by "they came," and to the grief that touched the Muslims. The meaning is: "do not think that disgrace will befall you because of it; rather it is good for you," for the clearing of innocence, the reward for patience over that harm, and the exposure of the slanderers' lie.**

**It was said that the address in "do not think it" is to the slanderers, and that it is good for them because this mention was a swift punishment like an expiation, and because some of them repented. This view is weak because of His later saying, "for every man among them is the requital of what he earned of sin," meaning the recompense of what he earned, which corresponds to the extent of his involvement in it: some of them laughed, some remained silent, and some spoke. "Iktasaba" (earned) is used for sins and the like, because it indicates effort and intention, so it is more emphatic in expressing responsibility. "Kasaba" is used for good, because its attainment suffices without indicating effort in it. "Kasaba" may also be used in both senses.**

Beware the edge of the sword from me, for I am a youth; when I am provoked, I am no poet.
But I defend my sanctuary and guard myself against the baseless liar who shoots at the innocent of appearances.

The wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance and the noble virtues.
The noble lady of the clan of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, whose noble endeavors and glory never fade.
Refined, whom Allah has perfumed in her chamber and purified from every blemish and falsehood.
If what was conveyed to you of me is what I said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And how could it be, when my love for her as long as I live, and my support, are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?
For him are ranks high above the people, whose excellence the assault of the boastful cannot reach.

And since they did not bring the witnesses, they are, with Allah, the liars.﴾ ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾ ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it a trivial matter, while with Allah it is grave.﴾ ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. **The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of these verses is well known and is recorded in the Sahih. Al-ifk means lying and fabrication. It was said: it is slander (buhtan) that you do not perceive until it suddenly surprises you. Al-'usbah means the group, and its discussion has already passed in Surat Yusuf (peace be upon him). The phrase "from among you" (minkum) means from among the people of your religion and those who belong to Islam; among them are hypocrites and among them are Muslims. Apparently, the predicate (khabar) of "inna" is "a group from among you," and "from among you" is in the position of a qualifier (sifah), as al-Hawfi and Abu al-Baqa said. The clause "do not think it" (la tahsabuhu) is a resumed sentence (mustaʾnaf). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "'usbah" is in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "jaa'u" (they came), and the predicate of "inna" is in His saying "do not think it," the estimate being "inna fi'l al-ladhina" (indeed, the act of those who...). This is more coherent in meaning and more beneficial than taking "'usbah" as the predicate of "inna." End of quotation.**

**The group is 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of hypocrisy; Zayd ibn Rifa'ah; Hassan ibn Thabit; Mistah ibn Uthathah; Hamnah bint Jahsh; and whoever supported them from among those whose names are not mentioned. The pronoun in "do not think it" apparently refers to the slander, and according to Ibn 'Atiyyah's parsing, it depends on the omitted element he estimated as the subject (ism) of "inna." It was said that it may refer to the slander, to the verbal noun implied by "they came," and to the grief that touched the Muslims. The meaning is: "do not think that disgrace will befall you because of it; rather it is good for you," for the clearing of innocence, the reward for patience over that harm, and the exposure of the slanderers' lie.**

**It was said that the address in "do not think it" is to the slanderers, and that it is good for them because this mention was a swift punishment like an expiation, and because some of them repented. This view is weak because of His later saying, "for every man among them is the requital of what he earned of sin," meaning the recompense of what he earned, which corresponds to the extent of his involvement in it: some of them laughed, some remained silent, and some spoke. "Kasaba" is used for good, because its attainment suffices without indicating effort in it. "Kasaba" may also be used in both senses.**

**"And for him who took upon himself its greater part" (wa-alladhi tawalla kibrahu): the well-known view is that this is 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and the great punishment is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was said that it is what befell Hassan of the loss of his sight and the paralysis of his hand, and that this came from 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy because of his persistence in enmity toward the Messenger (ﷺ) and his seizing of opportunities against him. A foul statement is reported from him about that; I have kept my book free from mentioning it and my pen from writing it. May Allah disfigure him. It was said that "the one who took upon himself its greater part" is Hassan, and the painful punishment is his blindness and his flogging (hadd), and Safwan's striking him on the head with a sword, and he said to him:**

Beware the edge of the sword from me, for I am a youth; when I am provoked, I am no poet.
But I defend my sanctuary and guard myself against the baseless liar who shoots at the innocent of appearances.

**Hassan recited lines praising the Mother of the Believers and showing his innocence of what was attributed to him. They are:**

Chaste and dignified, never suspected of any doubt, she wakes up hungry for the flesh of the heedless.
The wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance and the noble virtues.
The noble lady of the clan of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, whose noble endeavors and glory never fade.
Refined, whom Allah has perfumed in her chamber and purified from every blemish and falsehood.
If what was conveyed to you of me is what I said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And how could it be, when my love for her as long as I live, and my support, are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?
For him are ranks high above the people, whose excellence the assault of the boastful cannot reach.

**The well-known view is that Hassan, Mistah, and Hamnah were flogged. It was said that 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy was also flogged, and one of the poets of that age mentioned him in verse. It was said that Mistah was not flogged. It was said that 'Abdullah was not flogged. It was said that no one was flogged in this incident; but this contradicts the text.**

**"Flog them with eighty lashes" (fa-jlidūhum thamānīna jaldatan) [24:4]. Juxtapose this with the statement that the hadd (the prescribed punishment) is imposed only upon confession or evidence, and that its implementation is not restricted to reporting, just as the killing of the hypocrites is not restricted, though Allah has informed of their disbelief.**

**The majority (al-Jumhur) read "kibrahu" with a kasrah on the kaf. Al-Hasan, 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Zuhri, Abu Raja', Mujahid, Abu al-Barahsam, al-A'mash, Humayd, Ibn Abi 'Ablah, Sufyan al-Thawri, Yazid ibn Qutayb, Ya'qub, al-Za'farani, Ibn Miqsam, and Surah (from al-Kisa'i) read it. Mahbub (from Abu 'Amr) read it with a dammah on the kaf. "Al-kibr" and "al-kubr" are both verbal nouns of "kabura al-shay'," meaning the thing became great; but the Arabs' usage of the dammah is not for age. One says, "This is the kubr of the people," meaning their eldest in age or rank. In the hadith about the story of Huwayyisah and Muhayyisah: "The kubr, the kubr" (meaning: let the eldest speak). It was said that "kubruhu" with a dammah means most of it, and with a kasrah means the initiation of the slander. It was also said that with the kasrah it means the sin.**

**"Why, when you heard it" (lawla idh sami'tumuhu): this is an exhortation to think well, a rebuke, and an instruction in good conduct. Apparently the address is to the believers, excluding those who took upon themselves the greater part of it. It was said that they may be included in the address, and that there is in it a reproach, that is, denial was obligatory upon them. Then, after the address, the discourse shifted to the third person and from the pronoun to the explicit noun. The construction was not "you thought well of yourselves (bi-anfusikum khayran) and said" but rather it was done to intensify the rebuke through a shift (iltifat) in discourse, and to explicitly use the word "believers." This signifies that sharing in faith requires that no believer accept from a critic or slanderer a statement against his brother. It also indicates that when a believer hears a report about his brother, the right course is to base the matter on a good opinion, and to say, on the basis of that opinion, "This is a manifest lie," clearly affirming his brother's innocence, as one certain and aware of the true state of affairs would say. This is good conduct. As for "by themselves" (bi-anfusihim): it means that the excellent believing men and women should measure this matter against themselves; if it is far-fetched for them, they judge that it is even more far-fetched for one better than them. It was said that it means "by their mothers," and it was said "by their brothers," and it was said "by the people of their religion." He also said, "Do not find fault with yourselves" [49:11], and "greet one another" [24:61], meaning: let none of you find fault with another, and let some of you greet others.**

**"Why did they not bring four witnesses for it" (lawla ja'ū 'alayhi bi-arba'ati shuhada'): Allah made the distinction between a false accusation and a true one to be the presence or absence of four witnesses. If they do not bring them, then in Allah's judgment and law they are liars. This is a rebuke and censure of those who heard the slander and did not strive to repel and deny it, and an argument against them based on what is manifest and clear in the Law: that the accuser must be deemed a liar without evidence, and must be punished.**

**"Had it not been for Allah's bounty" (wa-lawla fadlu Allah): that is, in this world, through blessings, including the respite granted for repentance. "And His mercy upon you" refers to the Hereafter, through pardon and forgiveness. "Would have touched you" (lamassakum): the punishment for what you plunged into of the story of the slander. One says "afāḍa fī al-ḥadīth," "indafa'a," "hadaba," and "khāḍa," all meaning to plunge into speech.**

**"When you received it" (idh talaqqawnahu): the governing element (ʿāmil) for "idh" is "lamassakum." The majority read "talaqqawnahu" with a fatḥah on the three letters and a shaddah on the qāf. Al-Bazzi doubled the tā' and the Nahwiyyun and Hamzah assimilated (idghām) the dhāl of "idh" into the tā'. That is, one of you takes it from another. One says "talaqqā al-qawl," "talaqqanahu," and "talaqqafahu." The original form is "tatalaqqawnahu," and this is the reading of Ubayy. Ibn al-Sumayfa read "tulqūnahu" with a ḍammah on the tā' and qāf and a sukūn on the lām, the present tense of "alqā." From him also: "talqawnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and qāf and a sukūn on the lām, the present tense of "laqiya." 'A'ishah, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Isa, Ibn Ya'mur, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read with a fatḥah on the tā', a kasrah on the lām, and a ḍammah on the qāf, from the Arab saying "wa-laqa al-rajul," meaning he lied, as transmitted by the lexicographers. Ibn Sidah said: they brought a transitive verb as evidence for an intransitive one. But in my view he meant "yalqūnahu fīhi" (they throw it into it), the preposition having been dropped and the verb attached directly to the pronoun. Al-Tabari and others relate that this word is derived from "al-walaq," which is hastening with one thing after another, like number after number, or speech after speech. One says "walaqa fī sayrihi" if he hastened in his journey. He said: "Camels of 'Īs brought him from Syria, hastening (yaliq)." Ibn Aslam and Abu Ja'far read "ta'liqūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā', a hamzah with a sukūn after it, and a kasrah on the lām, from "al-alaq," which is lying. Ya'qub, in the transmission of al-Mazini, read "tilqūnahu" with a kasrah on the tā', a yā', and a fatḥah on the lām, as if it were the present tense of "waliqa" with a kasrah on the lām, just as they say "tijal," the present of "wijilta." Sufyan said: I heard my mother read "idh tathqafūnahu," meaning the present tense of "thaqifa." He said: her father used to read according to the letters of Ibn Mas'ud.**

**The meaning of "with your mouths" (bi-afwāhikum) is that you turn it over in them without knowledge, because a known matter resides in the heart and then the tongue expresses it; and this slander has no locus except the mouths, as He said: "They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts" [3:167].**

**"And you think it trivial" (wa-tahsabunahu hayyinan): that is, a small sin. "And it is with Allah" great, among the major sins. He attached the touching of punishment to three sins: receiving the slander, speaking it, and considering it trivial. Then He began rebuking them for speaking it, and it was obligatory upon them, when they heard it, not to utter it. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how is it permissible to separate "lawla" and "qultum" (you said)? I say: adverbs have a status, namely their placement among things as if they were the things themselves, since they occur within them and are not separate from them; so what is permissible in them is permissible in other things. End of quotation. What he mentioned about the particles of urging suggests that this is particular to adverbs, which is not so; rather it is permissible to front the object before the verb. You say "lawlā Zaydan ḍarabta" (why did you not strike Zayd) and "halla 'Amran qatalta" (why did you not kill 'Amr). Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit of fronting the adverb so that it becomes an intervening element? I say: the benefit is to show that it was obligatory upon them to refrain from speaking of the slander at the very moment they heard it. Since mention of the time is more important, fronting was required. If you ask, what is the meaning of "yakūnu" (it is/it befits), when the sentence without it would be "mā lanā an natakallama bi-hādhā" (it is not for us to speak of this)? I say: its meaning is "mā yanbaghī wa-yaṣiḥḥu," that is, "it is not fitting for us to speak of this, and it is not valid for us." Similarly, "mā yakūnu lī an aqūla mā laysa lī bi-ḥaqqin" (it is not for me to say what is not my right). "Subḥānaka" (Glory be to You) expresses wonder at the magnitude of the matter. If you ask, what is the meaning of wonder in the word of glorification? I say: the origin of that is that Allah is glorified when one sees something amazing among His creations; then it became common, until it was used for everything that is amazing. Or it is to declare Allah far above the violation of the sanctity of His Prophet (ﷺ), as was said regarding this matter. End of quotation.**

**"Allah admonishes you that you return" (yaʿiẓukumu Allāhu an taʿūdū): that is, concerning returning to it. One says, "I admonished so-and-so about such-and-such, and he left it."**

**"If you are believers" (in kuntum mu'minīn): an urging for them to take admonition and a stirring, because it is the nature of the believer to keep away from what disgraces him of ugly things. It was said that "an taʿūdū" (that you return) is an object of purpose (maf'ūl li-ajlihi), meaning: out of dislike of "an taʿūdū."**

Allah makes the signs clear to you, that is, the proofs of His knowledge and wisdom through what He sends down to you of legislation (shara'i'), and teaches you of good conduct (adab), and admonishes you with healing exhortations.

Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and in the Hereafter. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: the reference is to Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those who resemble him.

"Among those who believe" is due to their enmity toward them. The painful punishment in this world is the prescribed hadd (the fixed legal penalty), and in the Hereafter it is the Fire. The apparent meaning of "Those who love that indecency should spread" is general, covering every slanderer, whether a hypocrite or a believer. Attaching the threat to the love of its spreading is evidence that intending depravity is itself depravity. Allah knows who is innocent and who is guilty, and the inner secrets of affairs, and the wisdom behind His concealing you and the severity of the threat. Al-Hasan said: by this threat and curse He meant the hypocrites, who intended and loved to harm the Messenger (ﷺ), and that is disbelief, and its doer is cursed. Abu Muslim said: they are the hypocrites, whom Allah threatened with punishment in this world at the hands of the Messenger through striving against them, as in His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73]. Al-Karmani said: "Allah knows their lie, while you do not know it," because it is unseen. The answer to (law la, "if not") is omitted, meaning: He would have punished you.

"And that Allah is Compassionate" in exonerating you, "Merciful" in accepting the repentance of whoever repents among those who slandered. Ibn Abbas said: the address is to Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, but the apparent meaning is general.

'A'ishah, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Isa, Ibn Ya'mur, and Zayd ibn 'Ali read with a fatḥah on the tā', a kasrah on the lām, and a ḍammah on the qāf, from the Arab saying "wa-laqa al-rajul," meaning he lied, as transmitted by the lexicographers. Ibn Sidah said: they brought a transitive verb as evidence for an intransitive one. But in my view he meant "yalqūnahu fīhi" (they throw it into it), the preposition having been dropped and the verb attached directly to the pronoun. Al-Tabari and others relate that this word is derived from "al-walaq," which is hastening with one thing after another, like number after number, or speech after speech. One says "walaqa fī sayrihi" if he hastened in his journey. He said: "Camels of 'Īs brought him from Syria, hastening (yaliq)." Ibn Aslam and Abu Ja'far read "ta'liqūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā', a hamzah with a sukūn after it, and a kasrah on the lām, from "al-alaq," which is lying. Ya'qub, in the transmission of al-Mazini, read "tilqūnahu" with a kasrah on the tā', a yā', and a fatḥah on the lām, as if it were the present tense of "waliqa" with a kasrah on the lām, just as they say "tijal," the present of "wijilta." Sufyan said: I heard my mother read "idh tathqafūnahu," meaning the present tense of "thaqifa." He said: her father used to read according to the letters of Ibn Mas'ud.**

**The meaning of "with your mouths" (bi-afwāhikum) is that you turn it over in them without knowledge, because a known matter resides in the heart and then the tongue expresses it; and this slander has no locus except the mouths, as He said: "They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts" [3:167].**

**"And you think it trivial" (wa-tahsabunahu hayyinan): that is, a small sin. "And it is with Allah" great, among the major sins. He attached the touching of punishment to three sins: receiving the slander, speaking it, and considering it trivial. Then He began rebuking them for speaking it, and it was obligatory upon them, when they heard it, not to utter it. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how is it permissible to separate "lawla" and "qultum" (you said)? I say: adverbs have a status, namely their placement among things as if they were the things themselves, since they occur within them and are not separate from them; so what is permissible in them is permissible in other things. End of quotation. What he mentioned about the particles of urging suggests that this is particular to adverbs, which is not so; rather it is permissible to front the object before the verb. You say "lawlā Zaydan ḍarabta" (why did you not strike Zayd) and "halla 'Amran qatalta" (why did you not kill 'Amr). Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit of fronting the adverb so that it becomes an intervening element? I say: the benefit is to show that it was obligatory upon them to refrain from speaking of the slander at the very moment they heard it. Since mention of the time is more important, fronting was required. If you ask, what is the meaning of "yakūnu" (it is/it befits), when the sentence without it would be "mā lanā an natakallama bi-hādhā" (it is not for us to speak of this)? I say: its meaning is "mā yanbaghī wa-yaṣiḥḥu," that is, "it is not fitting for us to speak of this, and it is not valid for us." Similarly, "mā yakūnu lī an aqūla mā laysa lī bi-ḥaqqin" (it is not for me to say what is not my right). "Subḥānaka" (Glory be to You) expresses wonder at the magnitude of the matter. If you ask, what is the meaning of wonder in the word of glorification? I say: the origin of that is that Allah is glorified when one sees something amazing among His creations; then it became common, until it was used for everything that is amazing. Or it is to declare Allah far above the violation of the sanctity of His Prophet (ﷺ), as was said regarding this matter. End of quotation.**

**"Allah admonishes you that you return" (yaʿiẓukumu Allāhu an taʿūdū): that is, concerning returning to it. One says, "I admonished so-and-so about such-and-such, and he left it."**

**"If you are believers" (in kuntum mu'minīn): an urging for them to take admonition and a stirring, because it is the nature of the believer to keep away from what disgraces him of ugly things. It was said that "an taʿūdū" (that you return) is an object of purpose (maf'ūl li-ajlihi), meaning: out of dislike of "an taʿūdū."**

Allah makes the signs clear to you, that is, the proofs of His knowledge and wisdom through what He sends down to you of legislation (shara'i'), and teaches you of good conduct (adab), and admonishes you with healing exhortations.

Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and in the Hereafter. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: the reference is to Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those who resemble him.

"Among those who believe" is due to their enmity toward them. The painful punishment in this world is the prescribed hadd (the fixed legal penalty), and in the Hereafter it is the Fire. The apparent meaning of "Those who love that indecency should spread" is general, covering every slanderer, whether a hypocrite or a believer. Attaching the threat to the love of its spreading is evidence that intending depravity is itself depravity. Allah knows who is innocent and who is guilty, and the inner secrets of affairs, and the wisdom behind His concealing you and the severity of the threat. Al-Hasan said: by this threat and curse He meant the hypocrites, who intended and loved to harm the Messenger (ﷺ), and that is disbelief, and its doer is cursed. Abu Muslim said: they are the hypocrites, whom Allah threatened with punishment in this world at the hands of the Messenger through striving against them, as in His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73]. Al-Karmani said: "Allah knows their lie, while you do not know it," because it is unseen. The answer to (law la, "if not") is omitted, meaning: He would have punished you.

"And that Allah is Compassionate" in exonerating you, "Merciful" in accepting the repentance of whoever repents among those who slandered. Ibn Abbas said: the address is to Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah, but the apparent meaning is general.

The discussion of ﴿the footsteps of Satan﴾ has already preceded, both in tafsir (exegesis) and in recitation, in al-Baqarah. The pronoun in (فَإنَّهُ, *fa-innahu*, "for he") refers back to the conditional (مَن, *man*, "whoever"). That is: indeed, the one who follows the footsteps of Satan ﴿commands indecency﴾, which is what is extremely ugly (الفَحْشاءِ, *al-fahsha'*), ﴿and wrongdoing﴾ (المُنْكَرِ, *al-munkar*), which is what sound minds reject. That is, he becomes a leader in misguidance, such that he is a commander whom his followers obey.

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you, and His mercy﴾, through repentance that purifies sins, ﴿not one of you would have ever been purified.﴾ The majority of reciters read (ما زَكى, *ma zaka*) with the kaf lightened. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Abu Haywah, al-Hasan, al-A'mash, and Abu Ja'far, in one narration, and Ruh read it with the kaf doubled. Al-A'mash also inclined the vowel, and wrote (زَكى, *zaka*) with the lightened form and with a ya'. It is from the roots with waw, by way of anomaly, because it may be inclined, or according to the reading of the one who doubled the kaf.

﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ from among those for whom happiness has preceded, and whose righteous deed is a sign of that preceding, or whom He wills by accepting the sincere repentance. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their words, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their inner thoughts.

﴿And let not﴾ (ولا يَأْتَلِ, *wa la ya'tali*) is the present tense of (ائْتَلى, *i'talá*), a form of (افْتَعَلَ, *iftaʿala*), from (الألِيَّةِ, *al-aliyyah*), meaning an oath. It was said that its meaning is "to fall short," from (افْتَعَلَ, *iftaʿala*) of (ألَوْتُ, *alawtu*), "I fell short," and from it is ﴿they will not spare you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118]. And the poet's saying:

*"A man, as long as the breath of his soul remains, / will not reach the extremes of calamities, nor will he fall short."*

This is the view of Abu 'Ubaydah, and Abu Muslim preferred it. The well-known occasion of revelation is that Abu Bakr swore not to spend on Mistah and not to benefit him with any benefit. Ibn 'Ayyash and al-Dahhak said: a group of believers cut off their benefits from those who spoke in the slander, saying, "We will not maintain relations with one who spoke about it," so it was revealed concerning all of them. The verse encompasses whoever has this description. The majority read (﴿يَأْتَلِ﴾, *ya'tali*). ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAyyash ibn Rabiʿah, Abu Ja'far his client, Zayd ibn Aslam, and al-Hasan read (يَتَألَّ, *yata'allā*), the present tense of (تَألّى, *ta'allā*), with the meaning "he swore." The poet said:

*"Ibn Aws swore an oath that he would return me / to women as if they were camels' bridles."*

"The grace and the abundance" means wealth. Mistah was the son of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq's maternal aunt, may Allah be pleased with him, and he was among the emigrants and among those who witnessed Badr. What was attributed to him was calling Abu Bakr to not treat him well. So he and those in his situation were commanded to pardon and overlook. When Abu Bakr heard ﴿Would you not love that Allah forgive you?﴾, he said, "Yes, I love that Allah forgive me," and he restored his provision to Mistah, and said, "By Allah, I will never withdraw it." Abu Haywah, Ibn Qutayb, and Abu al-Barhasam read (أنْ تُؤْتُوا, *an tu'tū*), with the ta', by way of (الِالتِفاتِ, *al-iltifat*, a shift in grammatical person). This corresponds with ﴿Would you not love﴾, and ﴿that they give﴾ governs the verb in the negative mood. If it has the meaning of an oath, then the estimate is "disliking that they give," and "that they not give," so the (لا, *la*, "not") was omitted. If it has the meaning of "falling short," then the estimate is "in giving" or "from giving." ʿAbd Allah, al-Hasan, Sufyan ibn al-Husayn, and Asma' bint Yazid read (ولْتَعْفُوا ولْتَصْفَحُوا, *wal-ta'fū wal-tasfaḥū*), with the ta', as imperatives addressed to those present.

﴿Indeed, those who accuse﴾ is general in reference to accusers, and the two accusers are included in it by way of giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine (تَغْلِيبًا, *taghlīban*, a grammatical convention of giving precedence). And (المُحْصَناتِ, *al-muḥṣanāt*, "chaste women") apparently is general in reference to chaste women. Al-Nahhas said: among the best of what has been said about it is that it is general for all people, male and female, and that the estimate is "those who accuse the chaste souls," so the masculine and feminine are included. It was said: it is specific to those who spoke about them in the story of the slander. It was said: it is specific to the mothers of the believers and their most elevated in rank and majesty. On this view, it means that he (the slanderer) plunged into them, and it was collected with intent toward them and their daughters from among the women of the community who are described by those attributes of chastity, intellect, and faith, as the poet said:

*"Be to me from the aid of the Khubaybs, my fellow..."*

He means ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr and his partisans. (الغافِلاتِ, *al-ghafilat*, "the unsuspecting") means those who are pure in their breasts and clean in their hearts, in whom there is no cunning or deceit, because they have not experienced affairs and do not perceive what the experienced perceive, as the poet said:

*"I indeed amused myself with a playful girl / simple, who reveals to me her secrets."*

Likewise, the simple-minded among men, in the saying of the Prophet: "Most of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded."

﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾ for slandering chaste women. It was said: this exception is by repentance, and in this verse there is no exception. Ibn ʿAbbas reported that whoever plunged into the story of the slander and repented, his repentance would not be accepted. The correct view is that the threat in this verse is conditional on the absence of repentance, and there is no difference between disbelief and sinfulness, and that whoever repents is forgiven. It is fitting that this verse, as it was said, was revealed concerning the polytheists of Mecca: whenever a woman went out to Madinah as an emigrant, they slandered her and said, "She went out to commit fornication." Abu Hamzah al-Yamani said this, and it is supported by His saying: ﴿On the day their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them﴾. And Ibn ʿAbbas reported that it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who doubted the religion, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will know where it will not benefit him.

The governing element of ﴿on the day they testify﴾ is what the prepositional phrase and the object depend upon, namely (ولَهم, *wa lahum*, "and for them"). Al-Hawfi said that the governing element is (عَذابٌ, *ʿadhāb*, "punishment"), but this is not permissible, because it is described, except according to the view of the Kufans. The two Akhawan (Hamzah and al-Kisa'i), al-Za'farani, Ibn Miqsam, and Ibn Sa'dan read (يَشْهَدُ, *yashhadu*), with a ya' from below, because the feminine is metaphorical, and a separation occurred. The rest of the seven read it with the ta'. Since the heart of the disbeliever does not desire what they testify to, Allah makes the limbs, the tongues, the hands, and the feet speak of what they did in this world, and empowers them to do so. Life is not a condition for the existence of speech. The Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school) said: He creates speech in these limbs, and for them the speaker is the doer of speech, so that testimony is in truth from Allah, except that He, exalted is He, attributed it to the limbs by way of extension. They also said: He, exalted is He, creates these limbs in a state other than what they are in, and compels them to testify against the person and inform about his deeds. The judge (al-Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar) said: this is closer to the apparent meaning, because that indicates that they perform the act of testifying.

(يَوْمَئِذٍ, *yawmaʾidhin*, "on that day") is in the accusative governed by ﴿He will fully pay them﴾. The tanwin on (إذٍ, *idhin*) is a substitute for the omitted clause, and the estimate is "the day when they testify." Zayd ibn ʿAli read (﴿يُوفِيهِمُ﴾, *yūfīhim*) with a lightened form. Here (الدِّينُ, *al-dīn*) means recompense, that is, the recompense of their deeds. The poet said:

*"Nothing remained but the counting, / and if they repay them as they repaid..."*

From this comes the saying, "As you do, so shall it be done to you." The majority read (الحَقَّ, *al-ḥaqqa*, "the true") in the accusative as an adjective of (دِينَهُمُ, *dīnahum*). ʿAbd Allah, Mujahid, Abu Rawq, and Abu Haywah read it in the nominative, as an adjective of Allah, and it is permissible for the object to separate the relative pronoun from its modifier. And (يَعْلَمُونَ, *yaʿlamūna*, "they will know") to the end strengthens the view of those who said that the verse is about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, because every believer knows that ﴿Allah is the Truth, the Manifest﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you turned the whole Qur'an over and searched for what the sinners were threatened with, you would not find that God, exalted and majestic is He, has been more severe about anything than about the slander, and the frightening verses full of severe warning, grievous punishment, and harsh rebuke, and magnification of what was committed of this, and horror at what he undertook, which was revealed about it in various ways and precise styles, each of which is sufficient in its own domain. Had He revealed only these three, they would suffice, in that He made the slanderers cursed in both abodes together, and threatened them with a mighty punishment in the Hereafter, and that their tongues, hands, and feet testify against them for what they fabricated and falsely accused with, and that ﴿He will fully pay them﴾ the true recompense that they deserve, until they know in the presence of Allah that ﴿Allah is the Truth﴾. He was concise in that and elaborate, detailed and summarized, emphatic and repetitive, and brought what has not occurred in the threat against the polytheists who worship idols, except what is less than it in grievousness. End of quotation. This is a good statement. Then he said after some discussion: If you say, "What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿the Manifest Truth﴾?" I say: its meaning is the possessor of the manifest truth, the just one whose judgment has no injustice, and the one who is true and is not described as falsehood. Whoever has this attribute, the evil of an evildoer does not fall away from him, nor the goodness of a doer of good; so the right of such a one is that he be feared and his prohibitions be avoided. End of quotation. In his saying "the evil of an evildoer does not fall away from him," there is a hidden trace of Mu'tazilite doctrine (دَسِيسَةُ الِاعْتِزالِ, *dasīsat al-iʿtizāl*).

Apparently (الخَبِيثاتُ, *al-khabīthāt*, "the evil women") is a description of women, and likewise (الطَّيِّباتُ, *al-ṭayyibāt*, "the good women"), meaning: evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women. This is supported by its being contrasted with the masculine forms. The meaning is that evil women among women incline toward the evil of men, so this is close to His saying: ﴿The adulterer marries none but an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur: 3]. Likewise (الطَّيِّباتُ, *al-ṭayyibāt*) of women are ﴿for the good men﴾. This interpretation is indicated by the statement of ʿA'ishah when she mentioned the nine things that no woman was given except her: and at its end, "I was created good for a good man, I was promised forgiveness and a generous provision." Ibn Zayd took this interpretation, and it is a distinction between ʿAbd Allah and those like him, and the Messenger and his companions. So Allah did not make for him except every good woman, while those are evil, and they are the people of evil women. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: they are the statements and the actions. Then these differed. Some of them said: the evil words and deeds are not spoken or approved except by the evil people among men, so they belong to them and they belong to them in this respect. Others said: the words and deeds do not befit, and do not cling, when the slanderer throws and the accuser accuses, except to the evil people among men, so they belong to them and they belong to them in this respect.

(أُولَئِكَ, *ulāʾika*, "those") is a reference to the good people, or a reference to them and to the good women, if by them is meant women.

﴿Cleared of what they say﴾, that is: what the evil people say of evil words, or the accusers who throw accusations at chaste women, [and] He promised the good people forgiveness at the reckoning and a generous provision in Paradise.

The majority read (الحَقَّ, *al-ḥaqqa*, "the true") in the accusative as an adjective of (دِينَهُمُ, *dīnahum*). ʿAbd Allah, Mujahid, Abu Rawq, and Abu Haywah read it in the nominative, as an adjective of Allah, and it is permissible for the object to separate the relative pronoun from its modifier. And (يَعْلَمُونَ, *yaʿlamūna*, "they will know") to the end strengthens the view of those who said that the verse is about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, because every believer knows that ﴿Allah is the Truth, the Manifest﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you turned the whole Qur'an over and searched for what the sinners were threatened with, you would not find that God, exalted and majestic is He, has been more severe about anything than about the slander, and the frightening verses full of severe warning, grievous punishment, and harsh rebuke, and magnification of what was committed of this, and horror at what he undertook, which was revealed about it in various ways and precise styles, each of which is sufficient in its own domain. Had He revealed only these three, they would suffice, in that He made the slanderers cursed in both abodes together, and threatened them with a mighty punishment in the Hereafter, and that their tongues, hands, and feet testify against them for what they fabricated and falsely accused with, and that ﴿He will fully pay them﴾ the true recompense that they deserve, until they know in the presence of Allah that ﴿Allah is the Truth﴾. He was concise in that and elaborate, detailed and summarized, emphatic and repetitive, and brought what has not occurred in the threat against the polytheists who worship idols, except what is less than it in grievousness. End of quotation. This is a good statement. Then he said after some discussion: If you say, "What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿the Manifest Truth﴾?" I say: its meaning is the possessor of the manifest truth, the just one whose judgment has no injustice, and the one who is true and is not described as falsehood. Whoever has this attribute, the evil of an evildoer does not fall away from him, nor the goodness of a doer of good; so the right of such a one is that he be feared and his prohibitions be avoided. End of quotation. In his saying "the evil of an evildoer does not fall away from him," there is a hidden trace of Mu'tazilite doctrine (دَسِيسَةُ الِاعْتِزالِ, *dasīsat al-iʿtizāl*).

Apparently (الخَبِيثاتُ, *al-khabīthāt*, "the evil women") is a description of women, and likewise (الطَّيِّباتُ, *al-ṭayyibāt*, "the good women"), meaning: evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women. This is supported by its being contrasted with the masculine forms. The meaning is that evil women among women incline toward the evil of men, so this is close to His saying: ﴿The adulterer marries none but an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur: 3]. Likewise (الطَّيِّباتُ, *al-ṭayyibāt*) of women are ﴿for the good men﴾. This interpretation is indicated by the statement of ʿA'ishah when she mentioned the nine things that no woman was given except her: and at its end, "I was created good for a good man, I was promised forgiveness and a generous provision." Ibn Zayd took this interpretation, and it is a distinction between ʿAbd Allah and those like him, and the Messenger and his companions. So Allah did not make for him except every good woman, while those are evil, and they are the people of evil women. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: they are the statements and the actions. Then these differed. Some of them said: the evil words and deeds are not spoken or approved except by the evil people among men, so they belong to them and they belong to them in this respect. Others said: the words and deeds do not befit, and do not cling, when the slanderer throws and the accuser accuses, except to the evil people among men, so they belong to them and they belong to them in this respect.

(أُولَئِكَ, *ulāʾika*, "those") is a reference to the good people, or a reference to them and to the good women, if by them is meant women.

﴿Cleared of what they say﴾, that is: what the evil people say of evil words, or the accusers who throw accusations at chaste women, [and] He promised the good people forgiveness at the reckoning and a generous provision in Paradise.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 24, verses 27–31 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their people. That is better for you, that you may remember.﴾ ﴿And if you do not find anyone in them, do not enter them until permission is given to you. And if you are told, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾ ﴿There is no blame upon you for entering uninhabited houses in which there is provision for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾ ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do.﴾ ﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze, guard their private parts, and not display their adornment except what appears thereof, and that they should draw their head coverings over their chests, and not display their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, the fathers of their husbands, their sons, the sons of their husbands, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, their women, what their right hands possess, male attendants who have no physical desire, or children who have not yet attained awareness of women's private matters. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you may succeed.﴾ [al-Nur: 32] ﴿And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your slaves and maidservants. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.﴾ [al-Nur: 33] ﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those among your slaves who seek a writing of emancipation, write it for them if you know good in them, and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your maidservants to prostitution if they desire chastity, seeking the transient goods of worldly life. And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nur: 33] ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that are clear, and an example from those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the righteous.﴾ [al-Nur: 34] ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp within a glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither eastern nor western, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Nur: 35] ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned. In them He is glorified morning and evening.﴾ [al-Nur: 36] ﴿Men whom neither commerce nor trade distracts from the remembrance of Allah, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah. They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about.﴾ [al-Nur: 37] ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty. And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ [al-Nur: 38] ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert which the thirsty one thinks is water, until he comes to it and finds it to be nothing; and he finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in account.﴾ [al-Nur: 39] ﴿Or they are like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud: darknesses, one above another. If he extends his hand, he can barely see it. And whomever Allah has not granted light, for him there is no light.﴾ [al-Nur: 40] ﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrate all who are in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each knows its prayer and its glorification. And Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ [al-Nur: 41] ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.﴾ [al-Nur: 42] ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them heaped up, and you see the rain coming out from within them? And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in which is hail, striking with it whom He wills and averting it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning nearly takes away sight.﴾ [al-Nur: 43] ﴿Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those with insight.﴾ [al-Nur: 44] ﴿And Allah created every creature from water. Among them are those that move on their bellies, among them those that walk on two legs, and among them those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ [al-Nur: 45] ﴿We have certainly sent down distinct verses, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ [al-Nur: 46] ﴿And they say, "We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger and have obeyed," then a faction of them turns away after that. And those are not believers.﴾ [al-Nur: 47] ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a faction of them turn away.﴾ [al-Nur: 48] ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly.﴾ [al-Nur: 49] ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Nur: 50] ﴿The saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is only that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ [al-Nur: 51] ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah, and is mindful of Him, those are the attainers of success.﴾ [al-Nur: 52] ﴿And they swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that if you order them, they will go forth. Say, "Do not swear; obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do."﴾ [al-Nur: 53] ﴿Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance."﴾ [al-Nur: 54] ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth as He granted it to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Nur: 55] ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ [al-Nur: 56] ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape in the earth. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Nur: 57] ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not yet reached puberty ask your permission at three times: before the dawn prayer, when you put off your clothing at midday, and after the night prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. Upon you and upon them there is no blame beyond these, as you move about attending to one another. Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Nur: 58] ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them did. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Nur: 59] ﴿And as for women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage, there is no blame upon them for removing their outer garments without displaying adornment. But to refrain is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [al-Nur: 60] ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves for eating from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, your mothers, your brothers, your sisters, your paternal uncles, your paternal aunts, your maternal uncles, your maternal aunts, or from what you possess the keys to, or from the house of a friend, whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses, that you may understand.﴾ [al-Nur: 61] ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and, when they are with him on a matter of common concern, do not leave until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some matter of theirs, give permission to whom you will of them and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nur: 62] ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others. Allah already knows those among you who slip away covertly. So let those who oppose his order beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nur: 63] ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows your condition. And the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Nur: 64]

(p. 443) **Ghaḍḍ al-baṣar** (lowering the gaze): closing the eyelid over the eyelid so that seeing is prevented. The poet said:

*So lower your glance, for you are from Numayr; you have not reached Ka'b, nor Kilab.*

**Al-khumur**: the plural of **khimar**, which is the head covering that a woman casts over her head. It is a plural of abundance (jam' kathrah), on which it is analogically formed, and in the plural of paucity (jam' qillah) it is **akhmirah**, which is also analogical. The poet said:

*And you see the thick-haired [men] in their rows, like heads whose khumur have been cut off.*

**Al-jayb**: an opening in the neckline of a shirt, from which some of the body appears.

**Al-'awrah**: that which is guarded from being seen. It is predominantly used for a man's private parts.

**Al-mar'ah al-ayyim**: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: every male who has no female with him, and every female who has no male with her. Its form is **fa'īl**, like **layyin**. It is said: **āma**, **ta'īmu**. The poet said:

*Every man will be left alone by his wife, or she will be left alone by him.*

That is, he will be alone and become an unmarried person (ayyim). The analogical plural of it is **ayā'im**, like **sayā'id** as the plural of **sayyid**. Its plural on the pattern **fa'ālā** is preserved (maḥfūẓ) and not analogical.

**Al-bighā'**: fornication. It is said: the woman **baghat** (committed fornication), **tabghī bighā'an**, so she is **baghiyy**. It is specific to the fornication of women.

**Al-mishkāh**: a niche (kūwah) that is not a through-opening (ghayr al-nāfidhah). Al-Kalbi said: it is an Ethiopian word that was Arabicized.

**Al-zujājah**: a known manufactured substance (jawhar maṣnū'). The vowelling of the **zāy** with a **ḍammah** is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and with a **kasrah** or **fatḥah** is the dialect of Qays.

**Al-zayt**: the oil extracted from the seed of the olive tree.

Al-Kirmani said: the mirage (**sarāb**) is vapour that rises from the lowlands of the plains and then condenses. When sunlight reaches it, it resembles water from afar, but when a person approaches it, he does not see it as he saw it from a distance.

Al-Farra' said: **al-sarāb** is what clings to the ground. It is also said: it is the shimmer that is seen at midday in the heat of the desert, appearing to the viewer as flowing water, that is, running water. The poet said:

*When we restrained the war, your pledges were like the glimmer of a mirage over the wasteland, gleaming.*

And he said:

*Tall, the gleaming of the mirage.*

It is also said: **al-sarāb** is what is rippled (yuraqraqu) from the air in the midday heat in the open expanses of the flat land.

**Al-lujjī**: abundant in water. The **lujjah** of the sea is its greater part. It is **lujjī**, a relative form attributed to the **lujjah**.

**Al-wadq**: rain, both heavy and light. The poet said:

*No cloud has poured its rain, nor has any land grown green from its rain.*

Abu al-Ashhab al-'Uqayli said: it is lightning. From this is the saying of the poet:

*They raised a dust cloud and came out from it like the emerging of rain from the gaps of the clouds.*

**Al-wadq** is the verbal noun of **waddaqa al-saḥāb** (the cloud rained), **yadiqu wadqan**, and from it is **istawdaqtu al-faras** (I made the horse mount a mare).

**Al-barad**: known; it is pieces that have frozen, from which water melts through heat.

**Al-sanā**: a defective noun from the root with waw, meaning light. The poet said:

*Its brightness shines, or the lamps of a monk.*

It is said: **sanā yasnū sanā**. **Al-sanā** is also a plant used as medicine. **Al-sanā'** with a long vowel means elevation and loftiness. He said: **wasana** like **sanaqa**, **sanā'an** and **sanā**.

**Adh'āna lil-shay'**: he submitted to the thing, complied with it. Al-Zajjaj said: **al-idhān** is hastening together with obedience.

**Al-ḥayf**: deviation in judgment. It is said: **ḥāfa fī qaḍiyyatihi**, meaning he was unjust.

**Al-liwādh**: evasion from one thing to another in secret.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 24, verses 27–31 (part 2 of 3):

﴿O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. That is better for you, that you may remember.﴾ ﴿But if you find no one in them, do not enter them until you are given permission. And if you are told, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾ ﴿There is no blame upon you for entering uninhabited houses in which there is benefit for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾ ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Aware of what they do.﴾ ﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze, guard their private parts, and not display their adornment except what appears of it, and let them draw their head coverings over their chests, and not display their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, what their right hands possess, male attendants having no physical desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women.
